title: Golden CI: make spectator session-scoped to avoid per-test JVM spawns
description:
Every golden test launches a fresh spectator JVM via `mvn -q exec:java` in Mage.Client.Observer, then kills it after the test. This is the single biggest per-test cost:

- First test (mana_drain): 36-48s spectator startup (cold JVM + Maven)
- Subsequent tests: ~16-22s each (Maven overhead + JVM class loading)
- 10 tests x ~18s avg = ~186s total (27% of golden CI time)

The bridge and potato are already session-scoped. If the spectator could be reused across tests (like the bridge is), the 10 JVM startups would collapse to 1.

This requires Java changes to Mage.Client.Observer to support resetting state between games without restarting — creating a new table, re-watching, resetting the game directory, etc.

Evidence from recent CI runs:
- Run 22524763758: spectator_startup=184.0s (27.1%)
- Run 22517711462: spectator_startup=186.0s (26.7%)
- Run 22524555497: spectator_startup=198.0s (28.4%)

Expected savings: ~150s (~2.5 min). Highest single-change impact but requires the most Java work.
